```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_clarabel <- requireNamespace("clarabel", quietly = TRUE)
has_scip <- requireNamespace("scip", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(optcompR)
```

A conic program minimizes a linear (or convex quadratic) objective over the
intersection of an affine set with convex cones. Many convex problems that
are not linear or quadratic have exact conic forms: Euclidean norms,
geometric means, matrix eigenvalues, entropy and log-sum-exp. optcompR
supports four cones:

| Function | Cone | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `opt_soc_constraint(m, x, t)` | second-order | \(\|x\|_2 \le t\) |
| `opt_exp_cone(m, x, y, z)` | exponential | \(y e^{x/y} \le z,\ y > 0\) |
| `opt_pow_cone(m, x, y, z, alpha)` | power | \(x^\alpha y^{1-\alpha} \ge |z|,\ x, y \ge 0\) |
| `opt_psd_constraint(m, M)` | semidefinite | \(M \succeq 0\) |

Every argument must be affine in the decision variables once parameters are
substituted. A model with cones is classified as `"SOCP"` when all its cones
are second-order cones and as `"CONIC"` otherwise. Cones are convex sets, so
the model is convex when its objective is linear or a convex quadratic and its
rows are linear; that is recorded in the classification evidence.

Conic models are solved by [Clarabel](https://clarabel.org), an interior
point solver available from CRAN as the `clarabel` package. SCIP also accepts
second-order cones, which optcompR passes as the equivalent quadratic rows
\(\|x\|_2^2 \le t^2,\ t \ge 0\); that path also handles mixed-integer
second-order cone programs (`"MISOCP"`). A solver that does not support a
cone type is refused with a message naming the cone.

## Second-order cones

The distance from the origin to the line \(x_1 + x_2 = 2\) is
\(\sqrt{2}\). Minimize an epigraph variable `t` with \(\|x\|_2 \le t\):

```{r, eval = has_clarabel}
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 2)
t <- opt_variable(m, "t")
line <- opt_constraint(m, sum(x) == 2, name = "line")
opt_soc_constraint(m, x, t)
opt_objective(m, t)
opt_classify(m)
r <- opt_solve(m)
r$solver
opt_objective_value(r)
opt_value(r, x)
```

Row duals are shadow prices in the usual optcompR convention,
\(\partial f^* / \partial b\). Here \(f^*(b) = b / \sqrt{2}\), so the dual of
`line` is \(1/\sqrt{2}\):

```{r, eval = has_clarabel}
opt_dual(r, line)
1 / sqrt(2)
```

`opt_check()` verifies rows, bounds and cones at the returned point. The
cone residuals appear in `special`. The KKT check is skipped for conic models
because their multipliers live in the dual cones rather than on rows.

```{r, eval = has_clarabel}
d <- opt_check(r)
d
d$special
```

### A robust least squares fit

Second-order cones express norms of affine residuals. Minimizing
\(\|Ax - b\|_2\) exactly:

```{r, eval = has_clarabel}
set.seed(3)
A <- matrix(rnorm(40), 20)
b <- A %*% c(1, -2) + rnorm(20, sd = 0.1)
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 2)
t <- opt_variable(m, "t")
opt_soc_constraint(m, A %*% x - b, t)
opt_objective(m, t)
r <- opt_solve(m)
opt_value(r, x)
qr.solve(A, b)
```

The norm of the residual (not its square) is the objective, so the same
solution as ordinary least squares comes out, and the norm itself can now be
bounded, weighted or combined with other norms in one model.

## Semidefinite cones

`opt_psd_constraint()` takes a square affine matrix expression. Only its
upper triangle is used, so the matrix must be symmetric by construction.
`opt_sym_variable()` creates a symmetric matrix of decision variables with
\(k(k+1)/2\) underlying variables.

The largest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix \(A\) is the smallest \(t\) with
\(tI - A \succeq 0\):

```{r, eval = has_clarabel}
A <- matrix(c(2, 1, 0,
              1, 3, 1,
              0, 1, 1), 3)
m <- opt_model()
X <- opt_sym_variable(m, "X", 3)
t <- opt_variable(m, "t")
opt_constraint(m, X == t * diag(3) - A)
opt_psd_constraint(m, X)
opt_objective(m, t)
opt_objective_value(opt_solve(m))
max(eigen(A)$values)
```

A matrix built from expressions works too. The matrix
\(\begin{pmatrix}1 & x & 0\\ x & 1 & y\\ 0 & y & 1\end{pmatrix}\) is
positive semidefinite exactly when \(x^2 + y^2 \le 1\), so maximizing
\(x + y\) gives \(\sqrt 2\):

```{r, eval = has_clarabel}
m <- opt_model("max")
x <- opt_variable(m, "x")
y <- opt_variable(m, "y")
one <- 0 * x + 1
zero <- 0 * x
E <- c(one, x, zero, x, one, y, zero, y, one)
dim(E) <- c(3, 3)
opt_psd_constraint(m, E)
opt_objective(m, x + y)
opt_objective_value(opt_solve(m))
```

## Exponential cones

The exponential cone expresses \(e^x \le t\), \(\log\), entropy and
log-sum-exp. Minimizing \(t\) subject to \(e^x \le t\) and \(x \ge 1\) gives
\(e\):

```{r, eval = has_clarabel}
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", lower = 1)
t <- opt_variable(m, "t")
opt_exp_cone(m, x, 0 * x + 1, t)
opt_objective(m, t)
opt_objective_value(opt_solve(m))
exp(1)
```

Log-sum-exp \(\log \sum_i e^{a_i^\top x} \le s\) is the set of points with
\(\sum_i u_i \le 1\) and \(e^{a_i^\top x - s} \le u_i\), one exponential cone
per term:

```{r, eval = has_clarabel}
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x")
s <- opt_variable(m, "s")
u <- opt_variable(m, "u", dim = 3)
a <- c(1, -1, 0.5)
for (i in 1:3) opt_exp_cone(m, a[i] * x - s, 0 * x + 1, u[i])
opt_constraint(m, sum(u) <= 1)
opt_objective(m, s)
r <- opt_solve(m)
c(x = opt_value(r, x), lse = opt_objective_value(r))
f <- function(x) log(sum(exp(a * x)))
optimize(f, c(-5, 5))
```

## Power cones

The power cone with exponent \(\alpha\) bounds a weighted geometric mean.
With \(x + y \le 2\), the largest \(z\) with \(x^{0.3} y^{0.7} \ge |z|\) is
\(2 \cdot 0.3^{0.3} 0.7^{0.7}\):

```{r, eval = has_clarabel}
m <- opt_model("max")
x <- opt_variable(m, "x")
y <- opt_variable(m, "y")
z <- opt_variable(m, "z")
opt_constraint(m, x + y <= 2)
opt_pow_cone(m, x, y, z, alpha = 0.3)
opt_objective(m, z)
opt_objective_value(opt_solve(m))
2 * 0.3^0.3 * 0.7^0.7
```

## Mixed-integer second-order cones

With integer variables and only second-order cones the class is `"MISOCP"`,
which SCIP solves to global optimality:

```{r, eval = has_scip}
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 2, type = "integer", lower = -5, upper = 5)
t <- opt_variable(m, "t")
opt_soc_constraint(m, x - c(1.4, 2.6), t)
opt_objective(m, t)
opt_classify(m)$class
r <- opt_solve(m)
opt_value(r, x)
opt_objective_value(r)
```

## Accuracy

Interior point solvers stop at a relative tolerance near \(10^{-8}\). The
status `"almost_optimal"` means Clarabel stopped at a reduced accuracy; check
such points with `opt_check()` before relying on them. The reported bound is
Clarabel's dual objective, so `opt_objective_bound(r)` and the objective
together bracket the optimum.
